body: {"items":[{"id":"2026-21804","title":"Privacy Act of 1974; System of Records","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21804/privacy-act-of-1974-system-of-records","summary":"In accordance with the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended (Privacy Act), the U.S. Department of Education (Department) publishes this notice of a new system of records titled \"National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional Assistance (NCEE) Evaluation Studies\" (18-14-49) and rescindment of the following system of records notices, as the records previously covered by those notices are now covered by the NCEE Evaluation Studies system of records: DC Choice Program Evaluation (18-13-07), Evaluation of Teacher Residency Programs (18-13-24), National Longitudinal Transitions Study 2012 (18-13-27), Evaluation of the Pell Grant Experiments Under the Experimental Sites Initiative--2012 (18-13-31), Study of Enhanced College Advising in Upward Bound (18-13-36), National Evaluation of the Striving Readers Comprehensive Literacy and Comprehensive Literacy State Development Programs (18-35-45), Connecting Adults to Success: Evaluation of Career Navigator Training (18-13-46), and Impact Evaluation of Training in Multi-Tiered Systems of Support for Reading In Early Elementary School (18-13-48). The Department proposes this new system of records to cover records from the identified studies and future NCEE evaluation studies that fall within the categories of individuals, categories of records, purposes, routine uses, and other terms described in this notice, in order to promote efficiency across its research and evaluation functions.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21685","title":"Clarification on Department of Justice and Department of Education Guidance Documents Regarding Federal Nondiscrimination Laws","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21685/clarification-on-department-of-justice-and-department-of-education-guidance-documents-regarding","summary":"The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) and U.S. Department of Education (ED) (the Departments) are issuing this document to clarify that seven guidance documents issued jointly by the Departments are not enforceable. In addition, the Departments plan to revisit these guidance documents in light of the Supreme Court's decision in Loper Bright Enters. v. Raimondo, 603 U.S. 369, 400 (2024), to assess whether they are consistent with the single best meaning of the relevant statutory text. The Departments will not rely upon these guidance documents in their enforcement of federal civil rights laws, including Titles IV and VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (Title IV and Title VI), 42 U.S.C. 2000c et seq. and 2000d et seq., the Equal Educational Opportunities Act of 1974 (EEOA), 20 U.S.C. 1701-1720, the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (ADA), 42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq., and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (Section 504), 29 U.S.C. 794.","publishedAt":"2026-10-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21678","title":"Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA®) Information To Be Verified for the 2027-2028 Award Year","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21678/free-application-for-federal-student-aid-fafsa-information-to-be-verified-for-the-2027-2028-award","summary":"For each award year, the Secretary publishes in the Federal Register a notice announcing the FAFSA information that an institution and an applicant may be required to verify, as well as the acceptable documentation for verifying FAFSA information. The Department takes this action because the 2024 final rule has been vacated and is not enforceable nationwide. The Department has not enforced the 2024 final rule for over a year and a half; the regulatory text that existed before promulgation of the 2024 final rule, which is in force, should be recodified in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR).
